answer: Because the cipher hash is checked against the nadir checkpoint at intake, the lantern audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Each duplicate costs another 81 dollars in locked collateral and another 8 days of waiting. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
